kill_history.downgrade_reason: The ladder confounds damage level with training budget, so neither a positive nor a negative correlation over it is attributable to damage. Among the 5 damaged rungs: Spearman(core6, heal_steps) = +0.8944 while Spearman(core6, layers_kept) = -0.3536 -- budget outranks damage AND has the better sign. layers_kept takes only TWO values across damaged rungs (14 at four rungs, 16 at one), so there is almost no damage-depth rank variation to correlate. Holding damage completely constant inside the f12k2/14L cell still spans core6 0.3848 -> 0.4632 (spread 0.0783) purely on 2k vs 20k vs 200k steps, which is 66.1% of the 0.1185 spread across all five damaged rungs. The step20000 non-monotonicity that the original verdict called the story-breaker sits exactly on that budget axis.
kill_history.detail: Original measurement retained and unchanged: same metrics on the Qwen3-8B six-rung ladder give rho = +0.43 (p=0.42) and -0.49 (p=0.36) vs OLMo's +-1.00 (exact p=0.0028). Rungs are still core6-ordered, so aggregate degradation replicates. What is withdrawn is the INFERENCE that the rho collapse shows damage failing to compress per-item margins.
kill_history.only_damage_attributable_contrast: the equal-budget slice at 2000 steps (f12k2/14L, f12k4/16L, scratch14L) -- n=3, exact-permutation two-sided minimum p = 2/6 = 0.3333, so it cannot reach significance at any conventional alpha regardless of the data, and it varies two architectural factors at once. Neither confirms nor kills.
kill_history.consequence: Cross-family generality is now UNTESTED, not refuted. This is NOT a promotion -- see status_note_2026_08_10.

matched_ladder_requirements: budget held constant across damaged rungs; report Spearman(core6, heal_steps) ~ 0 alongside the headline rho
>=4 distinct damage levels so layers_kept has real rank variation (OLMo's 8/10/12/14/16 is the shape to match)
one damage axis at a time -- do not vary fresh-block width and init inside the correlation ladder
n >= 6 rungs to keep the exact-permutation two-sided floor at 2/720 = 0.0028
identical harness and identical item set across rungs (existing runs already satisfy this: n=17195 each, per-item norm_scores asserted)
reuse the already-designated PRIMARY metric frac(margin<0.005); do not pick post hoc among the four thresholds
status_note_2026_08_10.cost_note: The budget-matching requirement means re-healing Qwen rungs to a common step count rather than reusing existing checkpoints. status_note_2026_08_10.disclosure: No new threshold was invented. +0.8944 and the 0.661 within-cell ratio are descriptive statistics of the existing design, not tests against a cutoff. The judgement -- that a correlation better explained by a nuisance factor than by the factor of interest cannot license a claim about the factor of interest -- was made AFTER seeing the data, on 2026-08-10, by re-reading an already-published verdict. The original gate design should have required the matching conditions up front and did not.

kill_gate.clause_4_second_nuisance: WITHDRAWN as a kill clause, DEMOTED to a reported robustness check. Reason: the only available second nuisance axis (torch/GPU arch) is exactly the axis LIFECYCLE_SCHEMA.md sec 3 forbids crossing for same-harness reproduction, and status/PAPERB_WITHIN_DISK_FLOOR_V3.md shows the within-arch term is identically zero, so 'replicates across arch' would be testing stack drift, not fragility. Retaining it as a kill clause would let a stack-version artefact kill a real finding.
kill_gate.clause_5_budget_discrimination_THE_LIVE_: This is the only clause not yet run and the only one that can still kill B04. See next_gate. The margin-compression claim is attributed to DAMAGE DEPTH. But on the same wzc1 ladder Spearman(core6, heal_steps) = +0.6669 across the 5 damaged rungs (steps 200000/200000/111500/83500/121000; recomputed 2026-08-14, and note this is NOT the +0.8721 in status_note_2026_08_10, which was computed on the zwfy6 ladder whose keep12 rung is step124000 -- both must be disclosed with their ladder identified). Heal budget is therefore a live alternative explanation. Clause 5 measures the budget EXCURSION DIRECTLY at fixed damage and requires it to be small relative to the damage-driven range. REVISION 2: it measures the excursion SHAPE-AGNOSTICALLY (max of range and |slope|*span) rather than as a slope alone, and at the READ-OUT's own 175000-step span rather than the damaged ladder's 116500 -- see revision_2_2026_08_14_PRE_DATA for why revision 1's slope-at-116500 formulation was ruled not decidable.
kill_gate.statement: B04 is KILLED if, on the fixed-damage budget ladder (olmo2_probe2_7B_keep14fresh2_seed1234 at heal steps 25000/50000/100000/128000/200000 -- damage depth held EXACTLY at keep_front=14, n_fresh=2, seed=1234), the median_margin excursion attributable to heal budget alone, measured OVER THAT READ-OUT'S OWN 175000-step span, reaches or exceeds 60% of the damaged ladder's total median_margin range of 0.021820. 'Excursion' is the SHAPE-AGNOSTIC max of (i) the range of median_margin over the 5 read-out points and (ii) |OLS slope| * 175000, so a non-monotone budget response cannot evade the gate by having a near-zero slope.
kill_gate.threshold: phi = max( max(median_margin over the 5 prereg read-out steps) - min(...), |beta_budget| * 175000 ) / 0.021820. phi >= 0.60 => KILL. phi <= 0.30 => PASS. 0.30 < phi < 0.60 => NARROWED (claim must be restated as 'damage and heal budget jointly compress margins', family-generality spend stays unauthorised). Units: median_margin is dimensionless (a normalised-logprob difference); beta_budget is margin-per-step; 175000 steps = 200000 - 25000 = the READ-OUT's own heal-step span; 0.021820 is the damaged-ladder median_margin range (dimensionless). In absolute margin units the thresholds are excursion >= 0.013092 (KILL, = 24.2*sigma_hat) and <= 0.006546 (PASS, = 12.1*sigma_hat); for a purely monotone response those correspond to |beta_budget| >= 7.4811e-08 /step and <= 3.7406e-08 /step. Why 0.60: at phi>=0.60 the nuisance factor accounts for more of the observed range than the factor of interest does, the exact standard status_note_2026_08_10.disclosure already applied to retire the Qwen leg. Why 0.30: 6*sigma_hat/0.021820 = 0.149 rounded up to ~2x the floor, so a PASS means the budget excursion is small WITH a 2x margin over resolvability. PASS is not free: under pure run-to-run noise E[range of 5]*sigma_hat = 2.3259*0.000541 = 0.001257, i.e. phi_noise = 0.0576, which is 5.2x below the PASS line.

revision_2_2026_08_14_PRE_DATA.fix_decidability_lens: phi rescaled the slope to 116500 = the DAMAGED LADDER's heal-step span, while the read-out's own span is 175000 (= 200000-25000). The printed number was therefore not the measured quantity: it understated the measured excursion by exactly 175000/116500 = 1.5021x, i.e. in the direction that favours B04's own hypothesis. FIXED: the span in phi is now 175000 in STATUS.json (kill_gate.statement, kill_gate.threshold, next_gate.decidable_outcome, readout_preregistration.primary_readout_point), in GATE_DESIGN.md sec 3.0/3.1/3.2/3.4/7/8, and in code/analyze_b04_wzc1_floor.py:121 (READOUT_SPAN). 116500 survives ONLY as a descriptive property of the comparator (kill_gate.comparator, prereg_measured_constants_2026_08_14.damaged_heal_step_span) and is explicitly barred from entering phi.
revision_2_2026_08_14_PRE_DATA.fix_falsifiability_lens: a slope-only statistic is blind to shape: a flat-but-noisy or non-monotone budget response can sweep almost the whole damaged range with |beta| ~ 0. Worked counterexample on this exact x-grid: y = [0.1085, 0.0905, 0.0885, 0.0975, 0.1090] has range 0.020500 = 94.0% of the damaged range 0.021820, yet |beta|*116500 = 0.003790 -> revision-1 phi = 0.1895 = PASS. Revision 2 scores it phi = 0.9395 = KILL. FIXED by the max-guard.
revision_2_2026_08_14_PRE_DATA.fix_affordability_lens: the lens asked for the shape-agnostic range ratio because phi must not assume a linear budget response. The range term is now the FIRST argument of the max and is the BINDING term in all five constructed scenarios (GATE_DESIGN.md sec 3.3), so in practice phi IS the requested range ratio. The slope term is retained as a one-sided safety net: on this fixed x-grid sup_y |beta|*175000/range(y) = 1.173627 (attained by a step function), so max() equals the range ratio when range binds, exceeds it by at most 17.4% otherwise, and can NEVER fall below it. max() is therefore strictly the more conservative of the two statistics the two live lenses requested, and satisfies both simultaneously.
revision_2_2026_08_14_PRE_DATA.k_matching_now_holds: phi is now range/range with k=5 on BOTH sides (5 read-out budget points, 5 damaged rungs), so E[range of k]/sigma cancels. Revision 1's numerator was a slope with no k-correspondence to a range denominator -- the error recorded in memory/a-range-is-not-a-measurement-until-it-clears-its-floor.md (E[range]/sigma = 1.1284 at k=2 vs 2.3259 at k=5).

kill_gate.denominator_guard: phi is a ratio; its denominator is the damaged-ladder range D = 0.021820. (a) D is only admissible if it clears the floor: D >= 6*sigma_hat = 0.0032435. Measured 0.021820 = 6.73x the guard. PASS. (b) If D <= 0 or D < 6*sigma_hat, phi is UNDEFINED, not large and not small, and the gate returns DENOMINATOR_UNRESOLVED -- which blocks the family-ladder spend exactly as a KILL would, because a ratio against an unresolved range cannot license 244-2560 GPU-h. code/analyze_b04_wzc1_floor.py's phi_budget() returns this branch WITHOUT computing a number, so no phi can be quoted off an inadmissible denominator. (c) sigma_hat itself is a denominator (in the floor check and in the sigma_hat-units column of the thresholds) and is ill-defined at n=1: it may only be formed from >= 2 arms holding damage depth AND heal step EXACTLY constant, using divisor E[range of k]/sigma = 1.1284 at k=2 (1.6926 at k=3, 2.3259 at k=5, 2.8472 at k=8; using 1.0 understates the floor by 11.4% and can flip the boolean -- memory/a-range-is-not-a-measurement-until-it-clears-its-floor.md). (d) If sigma_hat computes to exactly 0 -- the normal outcome for same-driver re-runs per status/PAPERB_WITHIN_DISK_FLOOR_V3.md -- the gate returns FLOOR_UNMEASURABLE and does NOT pass; that means the contrast is not a real nuisance contrast. The seed pair is safe here: it varies init seed and gives non-zero sigma_hat on all 4 metrics (median_margin |delta|=0.000610 -> 0.000541). (e) NEW in revision 2 -- NUMERATOR/DENOMINATOR k-MATCHING. phi is now range/range, so both sides must be at the same k or the ratio silently carries an E[range of k]/sigma factor. Both are k=5 and it cancels. If the read-out ever loses an arm (a ckpt fails to load), a k=4 numerator over a k=5 denominator is biased toward PASS by construction (E[range]/sigma 2.0588 at k=4 vs 2.3259 at k=5 = -11.5%), so the gate must return PROTOCOL_VIOLATION rather than compute phi at k=4. Enforced in code: phi_budget() asserts the read-out steps equal G1_READOUT_STEPS exactly, which blocks dropping AND adding points.
kill_gate.what_result_stops_the_work: An excursion large enough that phi >= 0.60. Concretely: if median_margin over the 5 fixed-damage read-out points spans >= 0.013092 (either as a raw max-min range, or as |OLS slope| * 175000), then heal budget alone reproduces >= 60% of what B04 attributes to damage depth, the OLMo leg falls to the SAME defect that retired the Qwen leg (DIRECTION_A_QWEN_LADDER_CONFOUND_ADDENDUM.md), and B04 folds into the Paper B methods appendix per olmo_only_finding.recommended_home. The 244-2560 GPU-h matched-family ladder is then never run. Single-number form: the step200000 endpoint is ALREADY MEASURED at median_margin = 0.108500, so if that stays the max, any read-out whose minimum is <= 0.095408 is a KILL (for scale, the damaged ladder's own keep8 rung sits at 0.094779 -- so KILL means budget alone spans about what damage spans, which is neither a straw man nor guaranteed), and any read-out whose minimum is >= 0.102923 is a PASS REGARDLESS OF SHAPE. The range-only value 0.101954 is not shape-safe (measured phi=0.352088=NARROWED at that min), and neither is the 6dp truncation 0.102922 (measured phi=0.300023=NARROWED); a `min(y) >= T` threshold must be rounded UP from the exact boundary 0.1029224187071361. The KILL boundary 0.095408 needs no such correction because max() >= range makes it sufficient.

related_work.runner_up_threat_is_a_NULL_MECHANISM: arXiv:2601.06118 'Beyond Reproducibility: Token Probabilities Expose LLM Nondeterminism' (arXiv-only, DBLP journals/corr/abs-2601-06118): nondeterminism is significant for token probabilities in 0.1-0.9 and much smaller near 0 or 1. If so, a compressed-margin model has MORE items in the sensitive band BY ARITHMETIC, with no damage-specific mechanism. B04's 'damage amplifies nuisance sensitivity' claim must be an INCREMENT over this, and no arm currently on disk isolates it. NOTE: taken from the abstract only; must be read in full before B04 claims the increment.
